title: White Villages & Moorish Cities
summary: Eight nights from Málaga: the Alhambra in Granada, the Mezquita in Córdoba, Seville's palaces and two nights in the mountains around Ronda.

stages.title: Granada
stages.why: Two nights so the Alhambra gets a full, unhurried day.

stages.title: Córdoba
stages.why: Stay in the old town to walk to the Mezquita.

stages.title: Seville
stages.why: Pick a hotel with parking, or park once and walk.

stages.title: Serranía de Ronda
stages.why: Mountain town between the white villages and the gorge walk.

days.title: Arrival
days.text: From Málaga up into the Sierra Nevada foothills; sunset over the Alhambra from the Albaicín.
days.tip: Parking in the Albaicín is restricted; walk up from the centre.

days.title: The Alhambra
days.text: A full day for the palaces and gardens, then tapas in the old town.
days.tip: Alhambra tickets are timed and sell out weeks ahead.

days.title: To Córdoba
days.text: Through olive country with a stop in a baroque hill town.

days.title: Córdoba
days.text: The great mosque-cathedral in the morning and the caliphs' palace city in the afternoon.
days.tip: Medina Azahara is reached by a shuttle bus from the visitor centre.

days.title: To Seville
days.text: A short drive with a stop in a hilltop town of Roman roots.

days.title: Seville
days.text: Royal palace, the grand Plaza de España and an evening in Triana.
days.tip: Book Real Alcázar tickets online to skip the queue.

days.title: White villages
days.text: Into the Sierra de Grazalema: a village under a castle and one built into the rock.
days.tip: Mountain roads are narrow and winding: allow extra time.

days.title: Caminito del Rey
days.text: The famous boardwalk through the Gaitanes gorge, then the bridge over Ronda's gorge at sunset.
days.tip: Caminito del Rey needs a timed ticket; it is about a 1-hour drive from Ronda.

days.title: Departure
days.text: Down from the mountains to Málaga airport.
days.tip: Allow about 2 hours for the drive.

entries.title: Mirador de San Nicolás
entries.notes: The classic viewpoint over the Alhambra with the Sierra Nevada behind.

entries.title: Alhambra & Generalife
entries.notes: Nasrid palaces, fortress and gardens; the palaces have a fixed entry time on the ticket.

entries.title: Priego de Córdoba
entries.notes: Baroque churches, fountains and a whitewashed old quarter, the Barrio de la Villa.
entries.why: Called the jewel of Córdoba's baroque, but few foreign visitors stop.

entries.title: Mezquita-Catedral
entries.notes: A forest of striped arches with a cathedral built inside it.

entries.title: Medina Azahara
entries.notes: Ruins of a 10th-century palace city, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

entries.title: Carmona
entries.notes: Hilltop old town with Roman gates and a parador above the plain.
entries.why: Thirty minutes from Seville, with a fraction of the crowds.

entries.title: Real Alcázar
entries.notes: Royal palace in Mudéjar style with large gardens.

entries.title: Plaza de España
entries.notes: Huge 1929 square with tiled alcoves for every Spanish province.

entries.title: Zahara de la Sierra
entries.notes: White village below a Moorish castle, above a turquoise reservoir.

entries.title: Setenil de las Bodegas
entries.notes: Houses built under overhanging rock along the river gorge.
entries.why: Unlike any other white village; quiet before midday.

entries.title: Caminito del Rey
entries.notes: Boardwalk along the walls of the Gaitanes gorge, about 3 hours one way with a shuttle back.

entries.title: Puente Nuevo
entries.notes: 18th-century bridge across the 100-metre-deep El Tajo gorge.

extras.season: April is ideal: warm, green and before the summer heat. Easter week (Semana Santa) brings processions and higher prices.

bookBy.what: Hotels in Seville and Granada, especially around Easter.
Real Alcázar and Mezquita tickets online.

documents: Car hire booking and credit card

budget.includes: Accommodation, food, fuel, tolls and entry fees, per person per day.
budget.notes: City parking can add 20–30 EUR a night.

notes.text: Old-town centres in Granada, Córdoba and Seville have restricted traffic zones. Ask your hotel how to reach it by car.
